newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China buys 750,000/T of South Korean diesel in Apr.
newsitem.headline: China buys 750,000/T of South Korean diesel in Apr.

text.p: China has imported at least 750,000 tonnes of diesel from South Korea in April and would continue to boost imports from its neighbour in future, Chinese importers said on Friday.
"China has bought at least 25 cargoes of diesel from South Korea in April. Each cargo is around 30,000 tonnes," said a trader from a Chinese state oil trading firm.
"South Korean supplies are cheaper compared to Singapore," he said, citing lower freight costs between South Korea and China as one reason.

Chinese traders said freight costs to move a 30,000-tonne cargo of diesel from South Korea to China are estimated at between $190,000 and $200,000, compared with charges between Singapore and China which is at $210,000-$240,000.
A source with state trading firm SINOCHEM, said the company has already imported seven cargoes from South Korea for delivery to China in May.
He said South Korean supplies are also better in quality and SINOCHEM plans to raise imports from the country.
Diesel from South Korea is curently pegged at 30 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, Chinese traders said.
This is lower than prices of diesel supplied from Singapore which is assessed between 40 and 60 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, fob basis.

The trader said while Chinese diesel imports in May are expected to remain stable as in April, supplies from South Korea might be limited to around 20 cargoes due to maintenance shutdowns at Korean refineries.
Starting last year, South Korea has increasingly displaced Singapore's diesel exports to the mainland after boosting its refining capacity.
South Korean refining capacity rose to 2.44 million barrel per day by the end of 1996, from 1.82 million at the end of 1995.

Chinese traders said the bulk of diesel imports would be discharged at the port of Fujian in southern China. This signalled a shift in the shipping pattern, and posed a competition to cargoes from Singapore which were normally shipped to southern China.
Before this South Korean sellers normally unload their cargoes in northern Chinese ports such as Dalian.
Data released by Chinese customs last week, showed that China imported 793,252 tonnes of deisel in March.
On average, China imports around 600,000 tonnes of diesel a month.
